title: UOCAVA overseas/military ballot-transmission deadline — the 45-day date in Missouri's congressional-map fight
source: NEWS: the date is now verified against the statute itself rather than a party's brief — 52 U.S.C. § 20302(a)(8), read direct 2026-09-05 at law.cornell.edu and uscode.house.gov, requires a state to 'transmit a validly requested absentee ballot to an absent uniformed services voter or overseas voter — (A) except as provided in subsection (g), in the case in which the request is received at least 45 days before an election for Federal office, not later than 45 days before the election'; 2026-11-03 minus 45 days is exactly 2026-09-19 (computed, not asserted; it falls on a Saturday). This closes the first of the two estimate rationales originally filed here — the statute was previously known only through the Missouri Attorney General's emergency application in Hoskins v. von Glahn, No. 26A___ (filed 2026-09-04, ago.mo.gov, PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-05). Stays estimate on the second count, unchanged: this calendar has no confirmed source prefix for a statute or a court filing — the same mechanical gap recorded on missouri-map-ballot-deadline-2026-09-08 and midterm-elections-2026-11-03 — and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Understating the label only widens caution
notes: Proposed by the missouri-map-ballot-deadline-2026-09-08 initial research (2026-09-05) as the date that actually binds, after that research found the 09-08 entry mis-specified: 09-08 is a state ballot-administration deadline (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 115.125.2) that the applicant's own filing says the US Supreme Court 'is not bound by'. This is the federal one. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research, which corrected the characterisation while confirming the date: 09-19 is NOT a terminal date after which the map dispute goes moot. Section 20302(a)(8) is expressly subject to § 20302(g), whose undue-hardship grounds include 'The State has suffered a delay in generating ballots due to a legal contest' — Missouri's exact posture — with the Presidential designee (SecDef, delegated DoD/FVAP) deciding within 5 business days. The only precedent matching this fact pattern cuts both ways: Ohio requested that waiver on that ground 2022-02-26, was DENIED 2022-03-04, and then transmitted 17 days past its own 45-day date anyway under a DOJ memorandum of agreement that extended the ballot RETURN window by 20 days instead (US–Ohio MOA, DOJ Civil Rights Division, executed 2022-03-18, read direct 2026-09-05). UOCAVA is enforced by an Attorney General suit under 52 U.S.C. § 20307, not by a clock, so nothing self-executes on this date. Also note the verb: the statute says 'transmit', and practice permits electronic transmission at the voter's choice — not necessarily printed ballots in the post. Not a market event: symbols: [], the underlying 09-03 ruling drew no measurable index reaction (VIX 15.20 → 14.32 → 14.53 across 09-02→09-04), and 09-19 is a Saturday sitting one day after September opex and three days after the FOMC, so the date is structurally unobservable. Tracked as a seat-math input to midterm-elections-2026-11-03. Ledger: docs/research/events/missouri-uocava-ballot-mailing-2026-09-19.md
